summary: 1973 R-6 wooden cab on Red Mountain in the Patagonia Mountains; newest Coronado National Forest lookout, now semi-active and sharing the summit with radio equipment.

facts.design: Wooden R-6 flat-top dual cab, about 15 x 15 ft, with a roof overhang, on a 10 ft concrete foundation
facts.status_note: The register describes the lookout as in active service; a January 2020 summary calls it semi-active.

staffing.status: no staffing described; semi-active under the Sierra Vista Ranger District

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Coronado National Forest (Sierra Vista Ranger District)

visit.trail_note: Forest Road 4649 runs from Harshaw Road (Forest Road 58) south of Patagonia to the lookout. A 2010 hike log lists a distance of 6 miles and a gain of 2,000 ft.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR and FFLA entries both give US 452, AZ 45. They describe one lookout, so this is a match rather than a clash.

The register gives 5,758 ft (1,755 m), and the record keeps that figure. The 2020 summary and a 2010 hiking log both give 6,373 ft, which may refer to the road end or the summit rather than the cab. The sources do not say which.

notes_for_editor: Four sources, but the 2020 summary says it was compiled from the FFLA and NHLR websites, so it is not fully independent of them. Access: no source says whether visitors may enter the cab; the summary says the forest road ends at the lookout, and the 2010 hiker walked it. hikearizona.com returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Search snippets gave other hike distances (about 9 miles round trip) from pages I did not open, so they are not used. NHLR and FFLA coordinates differ by under 1 km. The NHLR line about listing until 2023 is not used. Access level is left out of facts because the sources do not state one.
